en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.10. Rootless Functional Indeterminate 2.1.10.1.
The Functional Mind-Element Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time the mind-element has arisen—which is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and is not the result of kamma; which is accompanied by equanimity;

and which has as its object a visible form … pe … a tangible object, or whatever else it may be directed toward—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate …pe….
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, three faculties, one contact …pe… one mind-element,
one mental-object base, and one mental-object element.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty;

or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time,
constitutes the aggregate of mental formations …pe….
These states are indeterminate (avyākata).
[They are] the functional mind-element (kiriyā-manodhātu). 2.1.10.2. The functional mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy (kiriyā-manoviññāṇadhātu-somanassasahagata).
Which phenomena are indeterminate?

At whatever time the mind-consciousness element has arisen—which is functional (kiriyā), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—accompanied by joy, having visible forms as its object, or ... pe ...
mental phenomena as its object, or whatever it may be directed toward—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception.
There is contact, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is rapture, there is pleasure,
there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of concentration,
there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of mental joy, and there is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What, at that time, is contact?
Whatever at that time is contact, touching, impingement, the state of having touched—
this, at that time, is contact …pe….
What, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind?

Whatever at that time is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of non-disturbed mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration, and the power of concentration of the mind—
this, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind.
What, at that time, is the faculty of energy?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort, the perseverance, the fortitude,
the steadfastness, the unfaltering persistence, the non-abandonment of zeal, the non-laying down of the burden, the grasping of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, and the power of energy— this is [the factor of enlightenment].
This, at that time, is the faculty of energy.
What, at that time, is the faculty of concentration?

That which, at that time, is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, and unperturbed state of mind; serenity, the faculty of concentration, and the power of concentration.
At that time, this is the faculty of concentration …pe… or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena there are at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate (avyākata).
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, five faculties, one contact …pe… one mind-consciousness element,
one mental-object base, and one mental-object element.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, formless states exist at that time—
these states are indeterminate …pe…. What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the life-faculty; or whatever other dependent,
immaterial states exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These states are indeterminate.
[They are] the functional mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy.
2.1.10.3. The functional mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity.
Which phenomena are indeterminate (*avyākata*)?

At whatever time the mental-consciousness-element (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) has arisen—being functional (*kiriya*), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—accompanied by equanimity, having visible form as its object, or ... pe ...
having mental phenomena as its object, or whatever else it may be directed toward—at that time there is contact (*phassa*), there is feeling (*vedanā*), there is perception (*saññā*).
There is feeling, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity,
there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of concentration, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity,
there is the life-faculty; or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [and so on] … At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, five faculties, one contact … [and so on] … one mind-consciousness element.
There is one base of mental phenomena (*dhammāyatana*), there is one element of mental phenomena (*dhammadhātu*);
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate (*abyākata*) …pe….
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the life-faculty;

or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial phenomena there are at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness.
At that time, this is the aggregate of formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*) … [as before] … these states are indeterminate (*abyākata*).
It is the functional mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity (*kiriyā manoviññāṇadhātu upekkhāsahagatā*).
Rootless functional [karma] is indeterminate.
2.1.10.4. Rooted Functional Karma of the Sense-Sphere.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time the mind-consciousness element has arisen, which is functional (kiriyā), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma,

accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge … [and so on].
Accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge …pe… accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge,
with volitional effort, having visible form as its object …pe… or having mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever it may be that has been taken up; at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe…
These states are indeterminate … [and so on] … non-greed is an indeterminate root … [and so on] … non-hatred is an indeterminate root … [and so on].
These states are indeterminate:
root-cause-associated sense-sphere functional states;
and fine-material-sphere functional states. 2.1.10.5. Fine-material-sphere functional states.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?

At whatever time one develops a form-sphere *jhāna* that is functional (*kiriya*), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma, for the sake of dwelling in happiness in this very life—secluded from sensual pleasures... [as before] ...one enters and dwells in the first *jhāna*.
The earth-kasina; at that time there is contact ... pe ... there is non-distraction ... pe ...
these states are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?

At whatever time one develops a form-sphere *jhāna* that is functional (*kiriya*), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—a pleasant abiding in this very life—then, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, ... [as before] ...
one enters and dwells in the second *jhāna*, ... the third *jhāna*, ... the fourth *jhāna*.
When one enters and dwells in the first jhāna …pe… the fifth jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa, at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are indeterminate.
Form-sphere functional [states].
2.1.10.6. Formless-sphere functional [states].
Which phenomena are indeterminate (avyākata)?

At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere jhāna that is functional (kiriya)— neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of kamma— a dwelling in happiness in this very life, which, through the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity, is accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite space, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere jhāna that is functional— neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of kamma— a dwelling in happiness in this very life, which, through the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity, is accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite consciousness, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere jhāna that is At that time, when one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on] … these states are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere *jhāna* that is functional (*kiriya*), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—
a dwelling in happiness in this very life— by completely transcending the base of infinite space, accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite consciousness,
and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … attains and dwells in the fourth *jhāna*, at that time there is contact.
There is [faith] …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are indeterminate (*avyākata*).
Which states are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere jhāna that is functional— neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of kamma—
a pleasant dwelling in this very life, which completely transcends the base of infinite consciousness and is accompanied by the perception of the base of nothingness;
having abandoned pleasure … [and so on] … one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna— at that time there is contact.
There is [mindfulness] …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?

At whatever time one develops a formless-sphere *jhāna* that is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of kamma—a pleasant abiding in this very life, which, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
and having abandoned pleasure … [as before] … enters and dwells in the fourth *jhāna*: at that time there is contact.
There is [faith] … non-distraction … these states are indeterminate … non-greed is an indeterminate root … [and so forth].
Non-hatred is an indeterminate root … non-delusion is an indeterminate root … these states are indeterminate.
Functional consciousness of the formless sphere.
Functional consciousness is indeterminate.
The Section on the Arising of Consciousness is finished.
